mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm employment (PAYEMS) signals strengthening labor market conditions and rising consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings growth accelerates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months where PAYEMS increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) reflects expanding manufacturing output and business investment, leading to higher corporate profits and positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth in the prior month fails to predict positive 60-day SPX returns with a Rank IC below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.8%, it signals a tight labor market that boosts consumer confidence and spending, causing immediate positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE falls below 4.8%.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.0% indicates a monetary tightening cycle that increases discount rates for equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of months with FEDFUNDS above 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in industrial production (INDPRO) and fall in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a robust economic expansion with strong labor market and production growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of INDPRO rising and UNRATE falling fails to predict positive 20-day SPX returns with a Rank IC below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) rise alongside accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% year-over-year), it signals demand-driven inflation that triggers aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: The interaction of rising HOUST and CPIAUCSL above 2.5% fails to predict negative 60-day SPX returns with a Rank IC below -0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS above 4.0% and rising for 3 consecutive months), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher discount rates and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of months during the monetary tightening cycle as defined by the trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: In a strong consumer demand phase (defined by RSAFS above 350,000 and HOUST above 2000), the S&P 500 tends to underperform over 60 days due to inflationary pressures and anticipated Federal Reserve rate hikes.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of months during the strong consumer demand phase as defined by the trigger condition.
